record.paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
record.context_brief: Basis conjecture for admissible Jack superpolynomials
record.original_question: Fix k≥1 and N≥k+1, and let F_N^(k) be the ideal of symmetric superpolynomials in N even variables x_1,…,x_N and N odd variables θ_1,…,θ_N over ℂ that vanish whenever x_1=x_2=⋯=x_{k+1}. For α_{k,2}=-(k+1), do the Jack superpolynomials P_Λ^(α_{k,2}) indexed by all (k,2,N)-admissible superpartitions Λ form a basis of F_N^(k)?

evidence.quote: Throughout this section, we set (3.47) α_{k,r} = -(k + 1)/(r - 1)
A superpartition Λ with exactly N parts is (k,r,N)-admissible if it satifies [32] (3.48) Λ^⊛_i − Λ^*_i+k ≥ r for all 1 ≤ i ≤ N − k

Let F^(k)_N denote the ideal of symmetric superpolynomials (over C) in N (even) variables x = x1, . . . , xN and in N (odd) variables θ = θ1, . . . , θN that satisfy (3.49) f(x, θ) = 0 whenever x1 = x2 = . . . = xk+1.
Conjecture 3.3 – The Jack superpolynomials P^(α_{k,2})_Λ(x1, . . . , xN, θ1, . . . , θN), with Λ (k, 2, N)-admissible, form a basis of the space F^(k)_N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the field $\mathbb{C}$. Let $N\ge 1$ and consider the superspace algebra in $N$ commuting variables $x_1,\dots,x_N$ and $N$ anticommuting (Grassmann) variables $	heta_1,\dots,	heta_N$, where $	heta_i	heta_j=-	heta_j	heta_i$ and $	heta_i^2=0$. The symmetric group $S_N$ acts diagonally by simultaneous permutation of $(x_i,	heta_i)$, and a superpolynomial $f(x,	heta)$ is called symmetric if it is invariant under this diagonal action. Denote the algebra of symmetric superpolynomials by $\mathcal{S}_N$.

A superpartition $\Lambda$ with exactly $N$ parts is a pair $\Lambda=(\Lambda^a;\Lambda^s)$ where $\Lambda^a=(\Lambda_1^a>\Lambda_2^a>\cdots>\Lambda_m^a\ge 0)$ is a strict partition (the antisymmetric/fermionic part) and $\Lambda^s=(\Lambda^s_1\ge\Lambda^s_2\ge\cdots\ge 0)$ is a partition (the symmetric/bosonic part), with the total number of (allowed-zero) parts equal to $N$. Associated to $\Lambda$ are two ordinary partitions, $\Lambda^*$ obtained by reordering the concatenation $(\Lambda^a,\Lambda^s)$ into a weakly decreasing sequence, and $\Lambda^\circledast$ obtained from $\Lambda^*$ by adding $1$ to each entry of $\Lambda^a$ before reordering. For fixed integers $k\ge 1$ and $r\ge 2$, $\Lambda$ is called $(k,r,N)$-admissible if
$$\Lambda_i^\circledast - \Lambda_{i+k}^* \ge r \qquad \text{for all } 1\le i\le N-k.$$

For a parameter $\alpha\in\mathbb{C}^\times$, let $P_\Lambda^{(\alpha)}(x_1,\dots,x_N,\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N)$ denote the Jack superpolynomial indexed by the superpartition $\Lambda$ (the unique simultaneous eigenfunction of the supersymmetric Calogero–Moser–Sutherland Hamiltonians with parameter $\alpha$ that is upper-triangular, in the dominance ordering on superpartitions, with respect to the basis of monomial symmetric superpolynomials, with leading monomial indexed by $\Lambda$).

Fix $k\ge 1$ and $N\ge k+1$, and set $\alpha_{k,2}=-(k+1)$. Let $F_N^{(k)}\subseteq\mathcal{S}_N$ be the ideal consisting of all symmetric superpolynomials $f(x,\theta)$ that vanish whenever $x_1=x_2=\cdots=x_{k+1}$.

Prove or disprove: the family
$$\bigl\{\, P_\Lambda^{(\alpha_{k,2})}(x_1,\dots,x_N,\theta_1,\dots,\theta_N) \;:\; \Lambda \text{ is } (k,2,N)\text{-admissible}\,\bigr\}$$
forms a $\mathbb{C}$-vector space basis of $F_N^{(k)}$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for results on the conjecture that Jack superpolynomials at α = −(k+1) indexed by (k,2,N)-admissible superpartitions form a basis of the vanishing ideal $F_N^{(k)}$ did not surface a definitive proof or disproof. Related work establishes clustering properties and connections with super-Virasoro ideals, but the basis statement itself does not appear to have been confirmed as resolved in the literature accessible via the search.

status_evidence.title: Jack Superpolynomials, Superpartition Ordering and Determinantal Formulas
status_evidence.snippet: Defines Jack superpolynomials as eigenfunctions decomposing triangularly with respect to superpartition ordering on monomial superfunctions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides foundational definitions for Jack superpolynomials but does not address the (k,2,N)-admissible basis conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Jack Polynomials as Fractional Quantum Hall States and the Betti Numbers of the (k + 1)-Equals Ideal
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Jack polynomial bases of the (k+1)-equals ideal in the non-super setting.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the analogous statement in the bosonic case but does not establish the superspace version.
